reason: A is the strongest composition across both text sizes and both states: the ball remains central, daily content stays open, and enlarged recovery copy fits. Baseline earns the higher populated screen score through its stronger artwork, navigation and supplied runtime evidence; A wins composition rather than implementation readiness. The coherent direction is A’s content arrangement with baseline’s illustrated depth and labeled navigation. No candidate meets the authorized threshold.
limitations: Independent assessment used only the attached images and supplied facts; no implementation, other ratings or runtime inspection.

Screen scores combine normal and 200% observations. Component vectors use hierarchy, typography/spacing, surfaces/color, clarity, feedback/recovery and accessibility; component averages normalize nulls using the same formula.

Null marks inapplicable typography-independent behavior or undemonstrated interactive prototype behavior, not a passing score. Prototype orb and tab interactions receive no inferred runtime credit; visible status and disclosure feedback remain assessable.
Baseline runtime evidence is accepted as supplied, not independently reproduced. It is not transferred to alternatives.
Content cutoffs are demonstrated viewport defects. Screenshots do not establish whether scrolling can recover that content, so no additional unreachable-content hard gate is asserted.

Prototype footer icons are ambiguous at normal size; enlarged labels crowd the available width. Navigation styling is assessed visually, while target sizes, semantics and activation remain unverified.
Physical iPhone, VoiceOver and native behavior remain unverified. These are provisional browser/design grades, not native certification; missing physical proof alone did not impose a numeric ceiling.
